parts.note: to initial a document is to sign it
A is the indefinite article
L stands for learner, the trainee driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner is told to point out where the opening article goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' reads as an adjective on 'article' but is the verb meaning to sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal something is to point it out or make it known, a straight synonym.

parts.note: read as an effortless rise up the career ladder, but meant as gentle, low-pressure advertising

explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' suggests a job step up; here it is marketing, and 'Easy' describes a gentle selling style.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle, persuasive sales approach is a mild form of advertising, as opposed to a pushy hard sell.

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means glossy and showy
an organ is a publication, a magazine or newspaper, speaking for a group

explanation.surface: A shiny magazine aimed at people who play cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMORGAN is a Welsh county with a first-class cricket club, so its players are cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorgan is the Welsh county club in English first-class cricket, so its team are cricketers.

clue.text: New backing for commercial European port

indicators.note: something backing another sits behind it, so the letter for new comes after the rest

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on television

explanation.surface: Fresh support for a business-minded port somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing for' puts N at the back, after AD and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a harbour city in Yemen, a well-known seaport.

clue.text: Public institute first to get going

indicators.note: says the word for institute comes first, before the word for public

parts.note: to institute something is to start it
something out is in the open, made public

explanation.surface: A public institution is the first to get under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public institute' reads as a noun phrase, but 'institute' is the verb meaning begin, and 'first' orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is to set off or begin, which is getting going.

definitions.meaning: a career that takes off suddenly becomes successful
to take an amount off a price is to discount it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: to become a sudden success, and to deduct from a price.

clue.text: Polite, but honour's not entirely satisfied

parts.note: to honour someone is to respect them

indicators.note: the word for satisfied is not given whole, losing its last letter

parts.note: after a big meal you are full, satisfied

explanation.surface: Someone is courteous, yet their sense of honour is not quite met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satisfied' reads as the surface's verb, but it is the adjective full; 'not entirely' drops its final letter to leave FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone courteous shows deference and good manners, so they are polite.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
mega is slang for brilliant or great

explanation.surface: A lover praises a splendid figure from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

parts.note: to treat a matter is to deal with it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Haggling over an arrangement with the head of a Yorkshire firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bargain' looks like a verb next to 'deal', but it is the noun, an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement struck between parties, a bargain on a grand scale.

definitions.meaning: to ... an animal is to trap it with no escape
a crook is a bend, as in the crook of an arm

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to hem someone in and an angle or bend, like a crook.

parts.note: the frame is the build or structure of the body
a work is a composition, such as a piece of music

explanation.surface: Sketching the make-up of a human figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' reads as the body's make-up, but it is a piece of art or music.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework is a basic structure or plan, an outline to be filled in.

indicators.note: to voice a word is to say it, so the word for recognised is heard

parts.note: something recognised has been seen and noticed

explanation.surface: A familiar voice gives an opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice' says that SEEN is spoken, which gives the sound of SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a view or vista, such as a rural landscape.

indicators.note: the word for dip is left without the letter for soft

parts.note: a dip in the ground is a slope
p, from piano, is the music abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A party dip without any soft fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'soft' is P, removed from SLOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloe is the small dark berry of the blackthorn, used in sloe gin.

clue.text: I learnt not to appear unduly prejudiced

indicators.note: the letters are arranged improperly, out of their due order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves not to seem too biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unduly' reads as part of the sense but signals the anagram of I LEARNT NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigoted person will not tolerate other views, being biased and narrow-minded.

parts.note: frank and straight both mean candid and direct
to be up is to be cheerful

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is cheerful, truthfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is the plain truth, sincerely, is said with this phrase as an adverb.

parts.note: to light on something is to spot it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the queen

explanation.surface: Catching sight of the queen's ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal vessel' reads as one phrase, but 'royal' is ER and 'vessel' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to ferry cargo to and from ships, a vessel.

definitions.meaning: more suitable or more capable, comparative of fit
someone who assembles or repairs machinery, such as a gas engineer

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of fit, more suited, and a tradesperson who installs machinery.

indicators.note: the word for shifty goes round the letters for ninety

parts.note: someone shifty is evasive, hard to pin down
XC is ninety in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dodgy character around ninety years old is confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifty' reads as a description of a person, but 'about' tells you to wrap that word around the Roman ninety.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive club limits its membership, so it is restricted.

definitions.meaning: to carry on is to have an affair, or to plot secretly
to interest someone is to arouse their curiosity

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to scheme or conduct a secret affair, and to fascinate someone.

definitions.meaning: an actor in a part is playing a role

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly, and read literally it describes an actor playing a role.

indicators.note: the two words joined together hold the letter a within them

parts.note: rent means torn, as in a garment rent apart
to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A rental scam involving someone who cheats tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid for housing, but it is the past participle of rend; 'involving' puts the A in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a whirlwind, the violent funnel of wind seen in the American Midwest.

clue.text: Stock company's name amounting to little

parts.note: stock is a broth, a kind of soup
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm's reputation adding up to not very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock company' reads as a business term, but 'Stock' is soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupçon is a tiny amount, a trace or hint of something.

indicators.note: a sound of a word is its spoken form, so the word for move is heard

parts.note: a step is a move, as in a dance

explanation.surface: A sensible manoeuvre, and simple too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound move' reads as a wise action, but 'Sound' marks the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland of Eurasia, a plain.

clue.text: Service man engaged in American battle

indicators.note: the service and man are placed inside the abbreviation for American

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A serviceman takes part in a fight in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service man' reads as one word, serviceman, but splits into a navy and a pronoun, which 'engaged in' places within the American abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnhem was the 1944 Second World War battle in the Netherlands, a famous airborne fight.

clue.text: Growth area Ron's agreed to develop

indicators.note: the letters are left to develop into a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken with its s, as written

explanation.surface: A development zone that Ron has approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth area' looks like business jargon but describes a plot where flowers grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose garden is a plot devoted to growing rosebushes, an area of plant growth.

definitions.meaning: a change, of position or direction
a simple loose dress or undergarment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a change, and also a loose straight dress.

clue.text: Problem coming back with right drill

indicators.note: the word for problem is read backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's there's the rub

explanation.surface: A problem returning with the correct drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns the problem word round to give BUR; 'rub' as a difficulty is from Hamlet's 'there's the rub'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a small rotary cutting bit, as on a dentist's drill.

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so the word for mane is sounded

parts.note: a mane is the long hair on a horse's or lion's neck

explanation.surface: A creature's mane, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says HAIR is spoken aloud, giving the sound of HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare is a long-eared field mammal, rather like a large rabbit.

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: A robbery in which a woman is shut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped' looks like the indicator but is part of the fodder: the answer sits inside 'sHE IS Trapped'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heist is a robbery, especially an armed raid, which is a hold-up.

clue.text: Winning legal case against occupying force

parts.note: an appeal is a case taken to a higher court
to be in a place or office is to occupy it
g is the symbol for the force of gravity

explanation.surface: Success in a lawsuit brought against an army of occupation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying force' reads as one army, but splits into IN and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning, as in a winning smile, means charming and attractive.

clue.text: Chap's caught the OAP out in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the title for a chap holds the rearranged letters within it

parts.note: Mr is the title used for a chap or man

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man has captured an old-age pensioner, in a figurative way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the pensioner phrase to ETAPHO, which 'caught' holds inside the title. OAP is British for old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech that describes one thing as another is a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Cancel tenancy held by British banker

indicators.note: the word for tenancy is held inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a British river, and a river has banks
a let is a lease or tenancy of property

explanation.surface: A British bank manager ends a lease agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' means a river, something with banks; the DEE flows in Scotland and on the Wales-England border.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or erase, so to cancel.
